_comment: Per-type floors, in percent of characters removed, measured through the HTTP
surface by e2e/runner/run_e2e.py. Keyed `type@mode`, plus `ALL@mode`.
These are set below the observed value on purpose. `make bench` already pins
the engine's ratio to four decimal places against a recorded
baseline; the job here is different — catch a change that breaks compression
*through the wire* while the engine still looks fine, which is a plumbing
failure rather than a tuning one. A floor tight enough to trip on tuning
noise would just get raised until it stopped meaning anything.
The rule, since 2026-09-26: no floor sits more than ~10pp below the observed
value, and a floor is never lowered. 10pp is far wider than tuning moves the
numbers and far narrower than a plumbing failure, which collapses a ratio
towards zero rather than shaving points off it.
That rule replaces a set of floors last chosen against a 240-payload corpus.
The engine had since improved enough that several gated on nothing at all:
text was floored at 11% against an observed 58.92%, and ALL at 48% against
70.04%. Raising a floor moves a gate, so the ones that moved are named here:
ALL 48→60, build 53/54→61, search 43/44→69, text 11/12→49, and the
8k-32k band 56/57→60. The rest were already inside the rule and were left
where they were — config, html, listing, source_code and the other two size
bands are all within 10pp already, html because it was retightened when the
fold-handle fix moved it.
Measured 2026-09-26 on the 257-payload shipped corpus:
type            n   aggressive  lossless  recoverable
size            n   aggressive  lossless  recoverable
ALL@recoverable agreeing with the README's headline 70.04% is the check that
the HTTP path and the engine path measure the same thing. If those two ever
disagree, this file is measuring something the engine is not.
A `size:<band>@<mode>` key floors a size band instead of a type. The corpus is
mostly small payloads while the large ones dominate the ALL average; without
these, a regression confined to the small majority passes. Bands stop at
>=32k: the harness truncates tool output near 40 KB, so nothing larger reaches
the engine. An earlier >=128k band was base64 image blocks.
Three types are deliberately unfloored, for three reasons.
diff: detection is right and three gates decline real agent patches — DESIGN.md 7.6.
json_array: n=1 on this corpus, so a floor would gate on a single payload.
tabular: no longer a bucket here at all — it was in the 2026-09-22 table and
the detector's prose-with-a-table problem is still open — docs/TABULAR.md.
2026-10-13: `text` was lowered 49→34, which the rule above forbids, so the
reason is recorded rather than the rule quietly dropped. 62 payloads were
added to the corpus that the engine *declines* — `untouched:text`, the
largest addressable skip bucket in the 89-task run of 2026-10-12 and 4x
under-weighted in the corpus before (BENCHMARK.md). This file buckets by
*detected* type, so those payloads land in `text` beside the ones a
compressor claims, and the bucket's average fell with no payload compressing
differently. `make bench` pins every engine bucket to four decimal places
against the recorded baseline and reports all of them unchanged, which is
the evidence that this is composition and not a regression.
The rule exists so a floor cannot be weakened to accommodate a regression.
It still holds for that. What moved here is the corpus, and a plumbing
failure — the thing this file is for — collapses a ratio towards zero rather
than shaving five points off it, so a floor at 34 catches it just as well.
Measured 2026-10-13 on the 359-payload shipped corpus, through the HTTP
surface, by this harness:
type            n   aggressive  lossless  recoverable
size            n   aggressive  lossless  recoverable
`size:<8k` is now the tight one: 36.82 against a floor of 34.0 in aggressive
is 2.8pp of margin where the rule asks for about 10. The added payloads are
all under 8 KB, so that band absorbed them too. It is left alone because it
passes and lowering a passing gate is not free; the next person to trip it
should read this paragraph before deciding it is a regression.
Measured 2026-10-25 on the 894-payload shipped corpus, through the HTTP
surface, by this harness:
type            n   aggressive  lossless  recoverable
size            n   aggressive  lossless  recoverable
The corpus grew from 359 to 894 payloads: 535 Claude Code tool outputs from
the Anthropic Harbor runs, kept with their declines as CONTRIBUTING asks. They
compress less than the Codex traffic before them — more short prose, more
source the agent is editing — so the averages fell with no compressor getting
worse: `make bench` compares payload by payload and none regressed, and
ALL@recoverable here still equals its 58.92% to the hundredth.
So two floors are lowered, and only because the thing they measure changed:
a floor is a fraction of a corpus, and this is a different corpus. ALL 60→55
in both modes and source_code 45/44→40 sit 4pp below the new values, inside
the 10pp rule. Two others moved up to stay inside it: config 57/56→70 (it had
drifted 21pp below) and the 8k-32k band 60→62 (10.8pp). The rest already
satisfy the rule on the new corpus. listing (78 against 78.88/79.20) and
`size:<8k` (34/33 against 34.71/34.38) are the tight ones now; both are
deterministic over a fixed corpus, so they trip on a change, not on noise.
tabular stays unfloored for the reason above, now with 25 payloads.
